categoryNote: Separate runtime subsystem (PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE section 7), not an install-time tweak set. Every entry here is preset-excluded: NX18 is user-optional and consent-gated, and the playbook's apply action only probes the capability (Get-Nx18Capability); a session is started exclusively by the user with Start-NxSession. All runtime mutations pass through the main journal via the existing engines (NX19 process scheduling, NX09 active power plan, NxApply registry pipeline), so main-journal rollback stays authoritative. Restore is verified-step only (a step that failed to apply is never restored) and only-if-ours. Protected process classes are hard-coded (NX18-012) and cannot be overridden by a profile. No background service is created by this build (PD-4 remains an owner decision); crash recovery is a manual/boot-time Invoke-NxSessionRecovery check. No entry makes a performance claim. Design references: docs/RESEARCH_RECONCILIATION.md adopt register 9/10 and r1-fsosx-xos.md, r6-hone-amewizard.md, r3-sapphire-vain.md (reference-only; implementation is original NEXTRIX code).

tweaks.name: Running game detection engine
tweaks.description: Detects whether a requested game image is running, from a read-only process table, and reports it with the launcher context. Detection only.
tweaks.objective: Give the session manager a truthful 'is the game running?' answer without touching, launching or terminating anything.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Resolve-Nx18GameIdentity normalizes a full path or an image name to an exact image name (wildcards refused). Find-Nx18GameProcess reads a process table: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process (ProcessId, ParentProcessId, Name, ExecutablePath) with a documented Get-Process fallback that reports parent ids as unavailable rather than inventing them. Matching is base-name equality against the requested image, and the result is a bounded list of PIDs. A protected image (NX18-012) is refused even at detection time, so a session can never be pointed at a launcher or an anti-cheat component. If no process matches, the caller may attach-wait for a bounded time; NEXTRIX never starts a game itself. A simulated table can be injected for drills and self-tests, so the detection path is verifiable without touching a live game. Read-only: no process handle is opened for write, no journal entry, no session record, no file is written.
tweaks.defaultState: No session subsystem; nothing observes game processes.
tweaks.proposedState: A read-only detection result (matched, image name, PIDs, launcher ancestors, reason) available to the session start path.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx18Capability -Capability NX18-001 returns implemented=true. Find-Nx18GameProcess -GameExe <name> returns readOnly=true and either matched=true with a bounded PID list (all PIDs whose image base name equals the requested name) or matched=false with a reason. A launcher or anti-cheat image name is refused. The self-test asserts both branches against an injected process table.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only detection; no state is written.

sideEffects: One read-only process enumeration per detection call.
No process, registry, service or file state is changed.
documentationSource: r1-fsosx-xos.md (game detection and R8 detection fixes; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Launcher & child-process relationship mapping
tweaks.description: Walks the parent-process chain of a detected game and reports which launcher owns it. Launchers are protected and never managed.
tweaks.objective: Explain the launcher context without ever steering, suspending or terminating the launcher or its helpers.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: The process table carries ParentProcessId (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process). Find-Nx18GameProcess builds an id-to-row lookup and walks up to ten ancestors per game PID, reporting every ancestor whose image name matches the Launcher class of the NX18-012 protected table (steam, steamwebhelper, EpicGamesLauncher, Battle.net, RiotClientServices, UbisoftConnect, EA Desktop/EADesktop, Origin). Ancestor names are matched through the same hard-coded guard, so the mapping and the protection cannot drift apart. No per-game EXE table is used (hardcoded game tables are on the rejected list): relationship is derived from the live parent chain. When parent ids are unavailable (Get-Process fallback) the mapping reports parentAvailable=false and asserts nothing. Trusted-launcher attach variants (a launcher that launches with different privilege or a separate client process) are NOT verified by this build and are not asserted; attaching to a game that a launcher started under another token is therefore Defined-by-detection only, never claimed. Read-only: no process is opened, no session record is written.
tweaks.proposedState: The game's launcher ancestors are reported and marked protected; the session never manages them.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx18LauncherMapping returns readOnly=true, managed=false and the Launcher-class entries. Find-Nx18GameProcess on an injected table where the game's parent is steamwebhelper reports exactly that ancestor as a launcher, and no launcher is ever returned as a management target.

sideEffects: Bounded ancestor walk (maximum 10 levels per game PID).
No process is touched.

tweaks.name: Game-specific session profiles
tweaks.description: User-authored per-game JSON profiles that declare the session's CPU-set profile, game priority, temporary power plan, allowlisted background apps and temporary graphics overlay.
tweaks.objective: Keep the per-game session definition declarative, reviewable and validated at the boundary, with no hidden defaults.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Profiles live under <SessionRoot>\profiles\<name>.json and are read by Read-Nx18Profile; this build never creates, repairs or writes a profile. The name is restricted to 64 characters without path separators or traversal. Test-Nx18Profile validates: schemaVersion 1; profileName matching the requested name; an optional game.exe that must not be a protected class; scheduling.cpuSetProfile in Competitive/Balanced/Streaming/Productivity (scheduling.applyAffinity is refused because affinity stays a separate opt-in NX19 mechanism); priority.gamePriorityClass restricted to Idle/BelowNormal/Normal/AboveNormal (High and RealTime refused by design); power.targetPlan length; at most 16 backgroundApps, each an exact image name that is not in the protected list, with priorityClass Idle/BelowNormal/Normal and mode PriorityTrim or BackgroundCpuSets; at most 8 graphics.registry overrides, restricted to HKCU:\ or HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ paths (never HKLM:\SYSTEM), DWord or String kinds, with SECURITY_POLICY banned value names (EnableLUA, VulnerableDriverBlocklistEnable, SaveZoneInformation, SmartScreenEnabled, mitigation overrides, PreventDeviceEncryption, Defender disable values) rejected. Duplicate allowlist entries and duplicate registry targets are rejected. A profile that declares no step is reported as a warning, not silently accepted as useful.
tweaks.defaultState: No session profiles exist; profiles are user-authored, never generated.
tweaks.proposedState: A validated per-game profile that the plan and session paths consume.

verify.procedure: Read-Nx18Profile -ProfileName <name> returns valid=true for a conforming file and valid=false with explicit issues for a protected background app, a banned registry value name, an HKLM:\SYSTEM path, High/RealTime game priority, or a traversal in the name. The self-test runs a valid and several invalid profiles from a temp folder.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - profiles are user files; the session manager never edits them.

originalState.method: The profile file itself is the declaration; nothing is captured or changed.

sideEffects: None on Windows configuration - validation is pure.
documentationSource: r6-hone-amewizard.md (per-session rules and exclusion lists; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Session CPU Sets application
tweaks.description: Applies an NX19-derived CPU Set selection to the game process for the duration of the session.
tweaks.objective: Steer the game onto a topology-derived CPU Set selection without hardcoded indexes and with a verified restore path.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: The plan derives the selection with New-NxCpuSetPlan (NX19-002) from the detected topology and the profile's scheduling.cpuSetProfile; the session never contains a literal logical-processor or CPU Set ID. If the topology or the LP-to-CPU-Set-ID map is unavailable, the step is Unavailable with the unresolved indexes and is not applied - no ID is fabricated. At apply time Set-Nx18SessionCpuSetStep re-checks the protected-process guard and delegates to Set-NxProcessCpuSets (NX19-003, targetType processCpuSets, journaled under NX18-004 before the API call). Microsoft documents CPU Sets as a soft mechanism; anti-cheat components may refuse or ignore it, which is reported and never bypassed. A step is added to the session's verifiedSteps list only when the engine's post-write read-back equals the selection. On exit the step is restored in reverse order through Invoke-Nx19Rollback with the NX18-004 filter (only-if-ours); a process that already ended needs no restore and is reported as ended-by-design. Session-scoped: no registry value, no persistence, no service.
tweaks.defaultState: The game runs with the OS-default CPU assignment.
tweaks.proposedState: During the session the game process carries the NX19-derived default CPU Set selection; the assignment ends with the process and is explicitly restored for a still-running process.

verify.procedure: The apply result must show verified=true for the process (NX19-003 re-reads SetProcessDefaultCpuSets state and compares sets). Get-NxProcessCpuSetState -ProcessName <game> before and after shows the changed default set; after session end it shows the recorded original set. The self-test asserts that a synthetic topology produces IDs from the NX19 map and that an unavailable topology yields an Unavailable step, never a literal index.

rollback.procedure: Session restore replays Invoke-Nx19Rollback -TweakId NX18-004 in reverse step order; only-if-ours at the process handle; a process that exited needs no restore. A crash is covered by Invoke-NxSessionRecovery (verified steps only) and by the main journal's NX18 category delegation.

originalState.method: Set-NxProcessCpuSets captures the process default CPU sets with GetSystemCpuSetInformation through a query handle before writing and journals them as targetType processCpuSets (cpuSetIds plus captureStatus). A process whose original state cannot be read is refused, not mutated.

sideEffects: CPU Set assignment is a soft affinity mechanism; anti-cheat may refuse or ignore it (reported, never bypassed).
Session-scoped only: the assignment ends with the process; no registry or persistent state changes.
documentationSource: r1-fsosx-xos.md (CPU Sets vs affinity and anti-cheat interaction; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Session power plan switching
tweaks.description: Switches the active power plan for the session and restores the recorded original plan on exit.
tweaks.objective: Provide a temporary power-plan context without overwriting the user's persistent plan choice.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-Nx18SessionPowerPlan delegates to Set-NxActivePowerPlan (NX09-001): the engine captures the active scheme GUID and name, journals the apply entry, runs powercfg /setactive, re-reads the active scheme, and records a verification entry. The session stores the returned original and modified GUIDs in its verifiedSteps list only when the switch verified. Restore is deliberately session-scoped rather than a replay of the NX09 category rollback: Restore-Nx18PowerPlanStep checks that the active scheme still equals the session's recorded target (only-if-ours); if the owner changed it during the session, the change is reported as diverged and left untouched. When it is still ours, it runs powercfg /setactive to the recorded original GUID, re-reads to verify, and journals the action as a rollback entry under NX18-005 (never as a new apply entry, so the main journal history stays clean and a later full rollback cannot switch back to the temporary plan). The original plan must still exist; it is never guessed from a stock default. If the plan name is unknown or the active scheme is unparseable, the step is skipped or refused before any switch.
tweaks.defaultState: The user's active power plan is unchanged.
tweaks.proposedState: During the session the profile's plan is active; on exit the exact recorded original scheme GUID is active again (or the divergence is reported).

verify.procedure: Get-NxActivePowerScheme after apply reports the session target GUID; after restore it reports the journaled original GUID. The session record's verifiedSteps entry carries that original GUID. Get-Nx18Capability -Capability NX18-005 returns implemented=true.

rollback.procedure: Stop-NxSession / normal exit / Invoke-NxSessionRecovery switch back to the recorded original GUID only when the active scheme is still the session target, verify by re-read, and journal a rollback entry. If the plan was deleted or the user changed plans, the divergence is reported and nothing is switched.

originalState.method: Set-NxActivePowerPlan records the active scheme GUID and name (targetType powerPlanSelection, AC/DC-independent selection) in the journal before switching; the session record stores the same pair in its verified step.

sideEffects: The active power plan changes for the duration of the session.
No other power setting is written; the original plan selection is restored only-if-ours.
documentationSource: r1-fsosx-xos.md (power plan switched back at session end; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Session background app management
tweaks.description: Priority-trims or CPU-set-steers explicitly allowlisted background applications for the session. Never terminates or suspends anything.
tweaks.objective: Reduce background scheduling interference only for apps the user named, with none of the blanket-termination patterns NEXTRIX rejects.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: The profile's backgroundApps array is the allowlist, and it is bounded (16 entries) and validated: every name must be an exact image name, must not be in the NX18-012 protected classes, and must be unique. Two modes exist: PriorityTrim (default) lowers the process priority class to Idle/BelowNormal/Normal through Set-NxProcessPriority (NX19-005, documented SetPriorityClass, journaled under NX18-006); BackgroundCpuSets steers the app onto the Background pool derived by NX19-002, and is marked Unavailable when that pool or its CPU Set IDs cannot be derived. There is no termination, no suspension, no service stop and no blanket process sweep: Set-Nx18SessionBackgroundTrim exposes terminationPerformed=false and suspensionPerformed=false and only calls the documented priority API. The protected guard is applied again at the apply dispatcher, so a profile edited after planning cannot smuggle a protected name through. Restore uses Invoke-Nx19Rollback with the NX18-006 filter (only-if-ours); an app that already exited needs no restore.
tweaks.defaultState: Allowlisted background apps run at their normal priority and CPU assignment.
tweaks.proposedState: During the session the named apps carry the requested lower priority class and/or the derived Background CPU Set pool; on exit their recorded original state is restored.

verify.procedure: Get-NxProcessCpuSetState (read-only) before/after shows the recorded priority class change for a named app; after session end it shows the original class. The self-test asserts that a protected app name is rejected at profile validation and again at the trim wrapper, and that the wrapper reports terminationPerformed=false and suspensionPerformed=false.

rollback.procedure: Session restore replays Invoke-Nx19Rollback -TweakId NX18-006 (processPriority and processCpuSets entries) in reverse order, only-if-ours. No process is ever killed to 'undo' a priority change.

originalState.method: Set-NxProcessPriority and Set-NxProcessCpuSets capture the original priority class / CPU sets through a query handle and journal them (processPriority / processCpuSets) before writing; an unreadable original refuses the mutation.

sideEffects: Only the named apps are affected; every non-allowlisted process is untouched.
No termination or suspension exists anywhere in this path (directive rule).
documentationSource: r6-hone-amewizard.md (per-session priority rules with an exclusion list; reference-only)
r1-fsosx-xos.md (Game Focus exclusion fixes for OBS/ShadowPlay; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Session service suspension (allowlisted)
tweaks.description: Defined capability for dependency-checked suspension of allowlisted services with automatic restore. Not shipped: this build never touches a service.
tweaks.objective: Reserve the design for temporary service suspension while refusing to ship an unsafe half-implementation.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Suspending a service for a session needs a journaled service-state engine that captures Start type, running state and dependencies, proves that nothing else depends on the service (or refuses when a dependent service is running), stops it, verifies the stop, and restores the exact original state on exit and after a crash. None of that engine exists in this build, so Get-Nx18ServiceSuspensionPlan is a read-only planner: it classifies requested names against the never-touch classes (security/Defender, audio, update stack, core services, recovery/VSS) and reports every service as not implemented with the reason. It performs no service query that changes state, no sc.exe call, no registry write, no journal entry. The catalogue's ADVANCED risk is retained, and the entry is preset-excluded with ExplicitConsent so it cannot be selected by accident. Shipping a stub that stops a service without the dependency/restore engine would violate the never-touch policy and the journal-first invariant, so the honest status is Defined.
tweaks.defaultState: All services keep their startup and running state during a session.
tweaks.proposedState: No service state changes in this build. A future build may suspend only explicitly allowlisted, dependency-checked, restorable services never in the never-touch classes.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx18Capability -Capability NX18-007 returns implemented=false. Get-Nx18ServiceSuspensionPlan -Services <names> returns readOnly=true, implemented=false, servicesTouched=0, and marks every requested service (including any never-touch class) eligible=false with a reason. Get-Service state is unchanged before/after (the function never calls it in mutation mode).

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no service state is changed by this build.

originalState.method: Not applicable - no mutation exists. A future engine must capture Start type, running state and dependencies before any stop.

sideEffects: None - the capability is plan-only and reports what it would refuse.
documentationSource: SECURITY_POLICY.md (never-touch services; service changes require journaled capture)
r4-synergy-ultraos.md (Start-only service undo with baseline diffing; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Session graphics configuration
tweaks.description: Applies a validated temporary per-game registry overlay (for example a per-app GPU preference) for the session and removes it only-if-ours on exit.
tweaks.objective: Allow a temporary per-game graphics context that composes existing tweak intent without overwriting persistent settings.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Session profiles may declare up to eight registry overrides. Each is validated at the boundary before anything is written: path must be under HKCU:\ or HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ (HKLM:\SYSTEM and ControlSet001/002 are refused), name must not be on the SECURITY_POLICY banned list, kind must be DWord or String, DWord values must be 0..4294967295, and duplicate targets are rejected. Application goes through Invoke-NxRegistryTweak, so the original value, type, value-existence and key-existence are captured and journaled under NX18-008 before the write, and the write is verified by re-read. This is the temporary composition path for graphics intent owned by NX04 (XREF NX04): the session does not duplicate NX04's static targets, and the plan shows the exact path/name/kind for review. Restore calls Invoke-NxRollback -TweakId NX18-008: reverse order, only-if-ours, exact original kind/value, values that never existed are deleted, and a divergence is reported rather than clobbered. The session never writes a persistent graphics setting; an overlay is temporary by construction.
tweaks.defaultState: No session overlay; persistent graphics values are untouched.
tweaks.proposedState: During the session the declared per-game overlay values exist and verify; on exit the exact original values (or value absence) are restored.

verify.procedure: Capture-NxRegistryValue before/after shows the overlay value; after session end it shows the journaled original value or absence. The self-test asserts that a banned value name, an HKLM:\SYSTEM path, a ControlSet001 path and a duplicate target are all rejected before any write.

rollback.procedure: Session restore calls Invoke-NxRollback -TweakId NX18-008 (reverse order, only-if-ours, exact kind/value, absent values deleted). The main journal can also restore the same entries if the session record is lost.

originalState.method: Invoke-NxRegistryTweak captures path, name, kind, value, value-existed and key-existed before writing and journals them (targetType registry).

sideEffects: Only the declared overlay values change, and they change only for the session's lifetime.
A value the user or another tool changes during the session is reported as diverged and left untouched.
documentationSource: PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE.md (section 3.5 conditional rollback and section 7 temporary configuration)
r1-fsosx-xos.md (GPU priority control per session, restored on exit; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Session process priority configuration
tweaks.description: Sets the game process priority class for the session using the documented SetPriorityClass path, restricted to Idle/BelowNormal/Normal/AboveNormal.
tweaks.objective: Offer a narrow, documented priority control for the game only, with none of the starvation risk of High or RealTime.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-Nx18SessionGamePriority re-checks the NX18-012 guard and delegates to Set-NxProcessPriority (NX19-005): the engine opens the process with query rights, captures the current priority class, journals a processPriority apply entry under NX18-009, calls SetPriorityClass, re-reads the class to verify, and journals the verification. High and RealTime are refused by the engine and by profile validation (they can starve system and input threads). The step is added to verifiedSteps only when the read-back equals the requested class. Only the game process named at start is targeted; no other process is touched. Restore replays Invoke-Nx19Rollback -TweakId NX18-009 with only-if-ours; a process that ended needs no restore. The change is session-scoped: no registry value, no persistence, no IFEO or image-hijack mechanism.
tweaks.defaultState: The game runs at Normal priority (the usual default).
tweaks.proposedState: During the session the game carries the requested priority class; on exit the recorded original class is restored.

verify.procedure: Get-NxProcessCpuSetState reports priorityClass equal to the requested class during the session and equal to the recorded original class afterwards. The self-test asserts that profile validation rejects High/RealTime and that the wrapper refuses a protected process name.

rollback.procedure: Session restore replays Invoke-Nx19Rollback -TweakId NX18-009, restoring the recorded original priority class only-if-ours; a dead process is reported as ended-by-design.

originalState.method: Set-NxProcessPriority reads GetPriorityClass through a query handle and journals priorityClass/priorityClassValue (targetType processPriority) before writing; an unreadable original refuses the mutation.

sideEffects: Priority classes above Normal are never used (no High/RealTime).
Session-scoped only; no registry or persistent scheduling change.

tweaks.name: Session journal & crash/interruption recovery
tweaks.description: Per-session state record plus a recovery check that replays restoration of outstanding verified steps after a crash, refusing on journal integrity errors.
tweaks.objective: Guarantee that an interrupted session is discoverable and that its still-applied steps can be restored without guessing.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Each session writes its own record at %ProgramData%\NEXTRIX\Sessions\session-<guid>.json with the state machine planned -> applied -> monitoring -> restoring -> completed | interrupted, a heartbeat per monitor cycle, the plan snapshot and a verifiedSteps list. Windows mutations themselves live in the main journal (NX19/NX09/NxApply engines), so the record is an index, not a second rollback authority. Invoke-NxSessionRecovery scans non-terminal records and, before touching any record, reads every journal it needs: if any journal reports an integrity error the whole recovery aborts with the errors and no record is modified (no partial restore). For each recoverable record it restores only entries in verifiedSteps, in reverse order, through the owning engine (only-if-ours); a step that failed to apply is not in the list and is never restored (FSOS-X R11 lesson). A record with no verified steps is closed as completed/Recovered. A record whose journal is missing is refused with that reason rather than guessed at. Restore failures leave the record interrupted so recovery can be retried; divergences are user-owned and are reported, not clobbered. No background service or scheduled task is created by this build; the recovery entry point is manual or boot-time (PD-4 is an owner decision). Records are treated as untrusted data: a record's journal root is honoured only when it lies under %ProgramData%\NEXTRIX (an explicit -JournalRoot always wins), so a tampered record cannot point an elevated recovery run at an arbitrary journal. The store inherits the %ProgramData% ACL (ACL tightening is the installer's responsibility, exactly as for the journal) and holds no personal data beyond the game image name and profile name.
tweaks.defaultState: No session record and no recovery path.
tweaks.proposedState: Every session leaves a final state record; an interrupted session is recovered from its verified steps with an explicit report.

verify.procedure: Invoke-NxSessionRecovery -WhatIf lists non-terminal records with their verified-step counts and touches nothing. On a real run: every non-terminal record ends completed or refused with a reason; the report shows restored/diverged/failed counts. Tamper test (self-test): after modifying a journal line, recovery returns aborted=true with integrityErrors and leaves every record's state unchanged.

rollback.procedure: The recovery run is the rollback path for an interrupted session. Session records are evidence and are never deleted by NEXTRIX; only their state is advanced.

originalState.method: The verifiedSteps list references the journal entries that captured the exact original state of each applied step; recovery never restores a step that has no verified journal-backed apply.

sideEffects: One small JSON record per session under the session root.
Recovery can switch the active power plan back and restore registry/process state; each action is journaled and verified.
documentationSource: r1-fsosx-xos.md (R11: a step that failed to apply is not restored; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Manual session control
tweaks.description: Start, stop and inspect sessions from the command line: plan preview, approval-gated start, manual end, status display.
tweaks.objective: Give the user one explicit, reviewable control surface with no automatic or hidden session.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Start-NxSession performs detection, profile validation, plan derivation, approval gating, journaled apply, a 2 s monitor loop with a heartbeat per cycle, and verified-step restore on exit. -Plan prints the plan and writes nothing (no session record, no journal entry, no directory). A real run requires -Approved, an already-running game (attach-wait for a bounded time; NEXTRIX never launches a game), an initialized journal, and an elapsed cooldown. Stop-NxSession ends a non-terminal session and restores its verified steps; an already-terminal session is a no-op. Get-NxSessionStatus reports one session (state, heartbeat age, stale flag while monitoring, verified-step count) or every stored session. A cooldown (default 90 s, recorded as cooldownUntilUnixMs) blocks rapid re-sessions after a session ends, following the FSOS-X R8 anti-cheat false-positive lesson. All mutation goes through the engines; this entry adds no mutation mechanism of its own.
tweaks.proposedState: A user can preview, start, monitor and stop a session explicitly, with the result recorded.

verify.procedure: Start-NxSession -Plan returns wrote=false and leaves the session root absent (self-test asserts it). A real start without -Approved throws; with an absent game process it throws after the attach-wait. Get-NxSessionStatus lists active and terminal records. Stop-NxSession on a terminal record reports alreadyTerminal=true with no restore.

rollback.procedure: Stop-NxSession restores verified steps; a normal exit does the same automatically. An interrupted process relies on Invoke-NxSessionRecovery.

originalState.method: Each applied step is captured by its engine before mutation and indexed in the session record's verifiedSteps list.

sideEffects: A session applies its plan for as long as the game runs (plus the monitor poll interval).
Rapid successive sessions are blocked for the cooldown period.
documentationSource: r1-fsosx-xos.md (R8 cooldown after anti-cheat false positives; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Protected-process policy guard
tweaks.description: Hard-coded guard that keeps anti-cheat, security, recording, audio, peripheral and launcher processes out of every session action.
tweaks.objective: Make the protected classes unbypassable by configuration, and prove it in tests.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: A single hard-coded table lists the protected classes: anti-cheat (EasyAntiCheat*, BEService*, vgk, vgc, Ricochet*), security (MsMpEng, SecurityHealthService, NisSrv, MpDefenderCoreService), recording (obs64, obs32, Nvidia Share*, AMD*RSServ*, Medal*), audio (audiodg, audiosrv), peripherals (iCUE, G HUB*, LGHUB*, Razer*, Logi*) and launchers (steam, steamwebhelper, EpicGamesLauncher, Battle.net*, RiotClientServices, UbisoftConnect*, EA Desktop*/EADesktop*, Origin*). Test-Nx18ProtectedProcess normalizes the image base name (path-safe) and matches wildcards case-insensitively; it has no allowlist or override parameter, so a user profile cannot override it. The guard is enforced at four points: profile validation (a protected background app or game name invalidates the profile), session start (a protected -GameExe is refused), the apply dispatcher (a protected process reaching a step throws), and the wrappers (Set-Nx18SessionCpuSetStep / Set-Nx18SessionGamePriority / Set-Nx18SessionBackgroundTrim refuse before any engine call). Launchers are identified for context (NX18-002) and are protected like every other class. The guard never terminates, suspends, re-prioritises or CPU-steers a protected process; there is no code path that does. The self-test runs a table-driven assertion over every class and over representative non-protected names.
tweaks.defaultState: No session subsystem exists; nothing is managed.
tweaks.proposedState: Every session action is filtered by the hard-coded protected list, with refusals reported.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx18ProtectedPolicy returns userOverrideAllowed=false and the six classes. Test-Nx18ProtectedProcess returns protected=true with the right category for representative names in every class, and protected=false for explorer/chrome/firefox/game names. The self-test is table-driven across all classes; a protected name in a profile is rejected by Test-Nx18Profile.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only policy; nothing is changed.

originalState.method: Not applicable - the table is code, not configuration.

sideEffects: A session refuses to manage a protected name; that refusal is the intended behaviour, not an error.
documentationSource: r6-hone-amewizard.md (exclusion lists protecting anti-cheat, recording, security; reference-only)
